reasons: Both answers explain the same-batch dependency, propose batch-level rejection of mutations, server-side precondition checks, iteration limits and error-as-observation handling. B gives concrete, runnable code for the ownership/status check in cancel_subscription, injects user_id and idempotency keys in the executor, and shows parallel_tool_calls=False in the actual call, while A's sketch leaves an unused has_write variable and relies on undefined helpers (request_confirmation, ToolError, session kwarg). B also correctly flags the cross-customer risk more sharply; A's extra point about the model possibly misreporting success to the user is useful but speculative.
